classification.classification_note: The metadata describes an out-of-bounds read in `parse_primitive` from missing 0-termination. Stage 01 reproduces that as an AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2 in `StrtolFixAndCheck` / `strtol`, with first project frame `parse_primitive:441`.

bug_description.original: An out-of-bounds (OOB) read occurs in the parse_primitive function in jplist due to missing 0-termination. The function parses integer and double values using strtoll and atof, which both expect the input string to be 0-terminated. If the JSON data is not well-formed and lacks proper termination, this can lead to OOB memory access and potentially cause a crash.
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the one-byte buffer `33` (`"3"`). In libplist's bundled jsmn tokenizer, `jsmn_parse_primitive` scans that byte, reaches end-of-buffer without seeing a delimiter, and still emits a `JSMN_PRIMITIVE` token with `start = 0`, `end = 1`. `plist_from_json` then dispatches the token to `parse_primitive`, which reconstructs `str_val = js + 0` and `str_end = js + 1` but passes `str_val` directly to `strtol`. Because the input buffer has length 1 and no NUL terminator inside the logical token span, `strtol` scans past the one-byte heap allocation while looking for a terminator or non-digit. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` in `StrtolFixAndCheck`, with `parse_primitive` line 441 as the first project frame. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by copying at most `str_end - str_val` bytes into a local buffer, appending `\0`, and parsing the terminated copy with `strtoll` / `atof`.

source.description: First project parser statement that materializes vulnerability-relevant state from the attacker-controlled JSON bytes: the primitive token boundaries later reconstructed as the numeric slice parsed by `parse_primitive`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` at `gt_results/arvo_44089/poc` has sha256 `4e07408562bedb8b60ce05c1decfe3ad16b72230967de01f640b7e4729b49fce` and contains exactly one byte `33` (`"3"`). `jsmn_parse_primitive` starts at offset 0, advances `parser->pos` to 1, and because it hit end-of-buffer rather than a delimiter, this statement emits a `JSMN_PRIMITIVE` token spanning `[0,1)` with no added terminator.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled one-byte numeric slice is first preserved here as token boundaries `start = 0`, `end = 1`; those offsets later become `str_val` and `str_end` in `parse_primitive`.

root_cause.description: The numeric parser passes `str_val` directly to `strtol` even though the only valid bound is the separate pointer `str_end`. No bounded copy or NUL termination is performed before using a C-string API that scans until a terminator or non-digit.
root_cause.note: The staged patch fixes this site by copying at most `str_end - str_val` bytes into `cbuf`, appending `\0`, calling `strtoll(cbuf, &endp, 10)`, and translating `endp` back to the original slice; it also switches the floating-point path from `atof(str_val)` to `atof(cbuf)`.

sink.description: ASan sink at the project call site. `strtol` interprets the one-byte token slice as a NUL-terminated string and over-reads the heap input buffer while searching for the byte after `'3'`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` `READ of size 2` in `StrtolFixAndCheck -> strtol -> parse_primitive`, and the invalid address is exactly one byte past a 1-byte region allocated by the libFuzzer runtime.

parser_admitted.description: After `jsmn_parse` succeeds on the one-byte buffer, top-level dispatch recognizes `tokens[0].type == JSMN_PRIMITIVE` and enters `parse_primitive` instead of rejecting the input as partial JSON.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness forwards the exact staged one-byte buffer `"3"` and its length 1 directly into `plist_from_json()`.
The bundled JSON tokenizer accepts the lone byte as a complete primitive ending at EOF and materializes token boundaries `[0,1)` without appending a terminator.

`parse_primitive` reconstructs a raw slice pointer from that token, takes the numeric branch for `'3'`, and calls `strtol` on the non-NUL-terminated slice, triggering the reproduced ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Source. For the exact one-byte witness `"3"`, the primitive scanner starts at `start = 0`, advances `parser->pos` to 1, and then leaves the loop because it hit end-of-buffer, not a delimiter or `\0`. This statement therefore emits a `JSMN_PRIMITIVE` token spanning `[0,1)` with no extra terminator byte.

`parse_primitive` converts the token from step 1 into a raw slice: `str_val` points to the first input byte, `str_end` points one byte later, and `str_len == 1`. The only bound on the numeric token is the separate pointer `str_end`; the slice is still not copied or NUL-terminated.
The only byte in the slice is `'3'`, so `isdigit(str_val[0])` is true and control enters the numeric parsing branch instead of the boolean/null branches.

Root cause. The numeric branch hands `str_val` to `strtol` as if it were a C string, even though the only proven extent is the one-byte slice ending at `str_end`. `strtol` gets no length argument, so nothing enforces the token boundary before scanning.

ASan sink. On the exact one-byte input, the interceptor reads two bytes while parsing the numeric C string, so the second byte falls immediately past the 1-byte heap testcase allocation. The saved stack is `StrtolFixAndCheck -> strtol -> parse_primitive -> plist_from_json -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

runtime_crash_location.function: StrtolFixAndCheck(void*, char const*, char**, char*, int)

crash_stack.function: StrtolFixAndCheck(void*, char const*, char**, char*, int)

poc.trigger: Stage 01 ran `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_44089 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/jplist_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` with first project frame `parse_primitive`.

format.name: single-byte JSON primitive buffer
format.contract: The exact staged witness must be the one-byte buffer `33` (`"3"`) with sha256 `4e07408562bedb8b60ce05c1decfe3ad16b72230967de01f640b7e4729b49fce`. It must reach `plist_from_json(json, length = 1)` with no additional delimiter or terminator inside the logical input span, so `jsmn_parse_primitive` emits `JSMN_PRIMITIVE` token `[0,1)` at EOF, `parse_primitive` takes the numeric branch on `isdigit(str_val[0])`, and the vulnerable call `strtol(str_val, &endp, 10)` treats that one-byte slice as a NUL-terminated string. No broader trigger class beyond this exact witnessed one-byte numeric JSON input is claimed.
